deep.reconstruction:
Setting. We are in a category C, probably a presheaf topos as in the 'Champs' / Pursuing Stacks circle of ideas. It carries:
- a class W of 'weak equivalences', assumed saturated;
- a class TC of 'trivial cofibrations'. TC is plausibly the saturated class (pushouts, transfinite composites, retracts) generated by a set of generating monomorphisms built from 'intervals' I, such as A×e → A×I;
- F = the maps with the right lifting property with respect to TC (fibrations);
- W~ = the weak equivalences of the closed model structure that TC, the cofibrations and F are meant to define.
The goal is to find conditions (1)–(5) on W guaranteeing W~ ⊂ W, i.e. that the model structure generated from the intervals does not invert more maps than W. It is a step toward W = W~, a closed model structure whose weak equivalences are exactly W.

Condition (2). We need A×e → A×I ∈ W for every A and every interval I in the given bounds. Since e → I has a retraction I → e, two-out-of-three (saturation) shows this is equivalent to A×I → A ∈ W for all A. That is, (I → e) ∈ UW, the class of universal (base-change stable) weak equivalences.

The main argument. We must show that saturating the generating maps into TC stays inside W.
- Factorisation. Take f: A → B in TC. By the small object argument, write f = p∘i with i: A ↪ B' in TC and p: B' → B in F.
- Why i ∈ W. The map i is built from generating maps by cobase changes and filtered (transfinite) colimits. So i ∈ W if:
  - (4) W is stable under filtered direct limits;
  - (3) monomorphisms in W are stable under cobase change.
  Grothendieck notes these are 'anyhow necessary for W = W~'.
- Retract argument. Hence every map factors as p∘i with p ∈ F and i ∈ TC∩W. For f ∈ TC, consider the lifting square with i on top, f on the left, p on the right and id_B at the bottom. Since f ∈ TC lifts against p ∈ F, there is s: B → B' with s∘f = i and p∘s = id. So f is a retract (direct factor) of i ∈ W.
- Condition (5). W must therefore be stable under retracts. Grothendieck flags this as not following from saturation in his sense, but as necessary for W = W~, since weak equivalences of a closed model structure are closed under retracts.

Conclusion: conditions (1)–(5) imply W~ ⊂ W. The two margin diagrams are exactly the lifting square and the retract diagram.
errors: 'Stability of W under filtering direct limits ... necessary for W = W~' is too strong in a general closed model category. Weak equivalences need not be closed under arbitrary filtered colimits; this holds e.g. in presheaf categories with monomorphisms as cofibrations (Cisinski) or for sufficiently large λ-filtered colimits in combinatorial settings. What is really necessary, and what the argument uses, is closure of TC∩W under transfinite composition and cobase change.

The remark that retract-stability is 'not a consequence of saturation' depends on the meaning of saturation. If W is strongly saturated (W = the maps inverted by C → W^{-1}C), closure under retracts does follow automatically. It is independent only for the weaker 'weak saturation' axioms (2-out-of-3 plus the idempotent condition). The reading of that parenthesis is also uncertain.
Condition (1) is not visible on this page (presumably on page 16, which is a computer listing in the scan, or earlier). So the full list (1)–(5) cannot be checked here.

ideas.what: Interval condition (I→e) ∈ UW, equivalently A×I → A ∈ W for all A, used to put the generating 'anodyne' maps A×e → A×I into W
ideas.modern_name: Homotopical interval / cylinder condition on a (basic) localizer; universal weak equivalences
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, Pursuing Stacks (1983) for localizers and UW; Cisinski (2002–2006) for the model-structure theory
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (localizers, intervals, 'universal weak equivalences'); Les Dérivateurs

ideas.what: Small object factorisation f = p∘i with i a trivial cofibration in W and p a fibration, followed by the retract argument (lift s with s∘f = i) showing a trivial cofibration is a retract of i
ideas.modern_name: Small object argument + retract argument (cofibrantly generated model structures)
ideas.where_published: Possibly in parts of Pursuing Stacks discussing closed model structures; not systematically

ideas.what: Sufficient conditions on a class W (saturation, interval condition, stability under filtered colimits, cobase change of monos in W, retracts) so that the model structure generated by intervals has W~ ⊂ W, aiming at W = W~
ideas.modern_name: Cisinski's theorem: every accessible localizer in a presheaf topos with monos as cofibrations is the class of weak equivalences of a cofibrantly generated model structure; Jardine-style 'cardinality' arguments
ideas.usually_credited_to: D.-C. Cisinski (2002 thesis; Astérisque 308, 2006); also Jardine, Beke, J. Smith for related recognition theorems
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks poses the question of whether modelizing localizers come from closed model structures; this precise sketch is not known to be published

missed.claim: Already in the 1982 'Champs' notes, i.e. before Pursuing Stacks, Grothendieck sketches the strategy for showing that a localizer W satisfying saturation, an interval condition, stability under filtered colimits, stability of monos in W under cobase change, and closure under retracts coincides with the weak equivalences of an interval-generated closed model structure. He proves the inclusion W~ ⊂ W via small object factorisation and the retract argument. This is essentially the first half of what Cisinski later proved.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck had the model-categorical approach to localizers (later Cisinski's theory) in mind earlier and more explicitly than the published Pursuing Stacks record suggests. The mathematics itself is now standard, so the interest is historical.

deep.surprise_reason: The arguments (small object argument, retract argument, closure conditions) are standard. The interest is historical: an explicit pre-Pursuing-Stacks sketch of the Cisinski-type comparison between a localizer and an interval-generated model structure, including Grothendieck's explicit list of necessary conditions. Nothing here goes beyond Cisinski's published theory.
transcription_corrections: Line under (4)/(3): the crossed-out phrase and the boxed phrase read 'monomorphisms in W by cobase extension' (W stable under cobase change of monomorphisms in W), not 'isomorphisms in W'.

'stability of W under (filtering direct) limits' – the inserted words are 'filtering direct', giving 'filtering direct limits'; label (4) is attached to this condition, label (3) to the cobase-change condition.
'This is equivalent to ... assuming' likely reads 'This is equivalent to assuming A×I → A is in W (using saturation)'.
'Thus any f) map factors' should read 'Thus any map f factors'.
The margin text near (3) is uncertain; possibly 'by transfinite limit exp' (expressing i as a transfinite composite), not 'by weak limit exp'.

Margin diagrams: the first is the lifting square A –i (W and TC)→ B', p ∈ F down to B, f: A → B in TC, with the section s: B → B'; the second is the retract diagram expressing f as a direct factor of i.
'Thus we need (4)' is uncertain; it could be 'Thus we need' followed directly by condition (5).
